metadata.description: Comprehensive VLSI Physical Design Error & Fix Knowledge Base

rules.explanation: High routing congestion detected. Lowering core utilization and placement density allocates more routing tracks. Increasing GRT adjustment loosens congestion weighting during global route.

error_keywords: net forced too close to macro
rules.explanation: Routing guides are too tight near macro boundaries. Increasing macro halo/channel width gives the router more clearance, preventing nets from being forced into congested narrow channels adjacent to macros.

Detailed router (TritonRoute) failed to complete all connections. Increasing iteration count gives more attempts to resolve conflicts. If it persists, address upstream congestion by reducing placement density.

All available routing layers are congested. Allow routing on higher metal layers and increase GRT adjustment to spread routing. Verify PDN straps are not consuming too many routing tracks on specific layers.

OpenLane.GRT_LAYER_ADJUSTMENTS: increase adjustment for blocked layer (e.g. li:0.99,met1:0.5,met2:0.5,...)

rules.explanation: Macros with internal routing on certain layers create obstructions. Increase the global routing adjustment on blocked layers to route signals around macros. Use macro halos to prevent cell placement competing for those routing resources.

OpenLane.SYNTH_STRATEGY: try DELAY 0, DELAY 1, DELAY 2, or DELAY 3

rules.explanation: Setup timing violated. Data path logic is too deep for this frequency. Relaxing the clock period, enabling resizer timing optimizations, or switching synthesis strategy (DELAY 0-3) can fix WNS/TNS.

High fanout nets create large load capacitance, increasing driver delay and causing setup violations. Reduce SYNTH_MAX_FANOUT so Yosys inserts buffers earlier. Upsize under-driven buffer cells using OpenSTA replace_cell.

After CTS, insertion delay introduced by clock buffers can worsen setup slack. Use stronger root clock buffers and verify clock path delay. Positive useful skew gives more setup margin on critical paths.
Hold violations mean data arrives too soon after the clock edge. The resizer fixes hold by inserting delay buffers on short paths. Enable hold fixing post-CTS with an appropriate slack margin.

error_keywords: hold violation due to clock skew

adjustments.useful_skew: apply negative skew on violating paths

rules.explanation: Positive clock skew worsens hold. Apply negative useful skew on paths with hold violations. Hold margin = hold_time + skew; negative skew directly increases the hold margin.

Slow signal transitions violate max slew/transition constraints. The resizer fixes these by inserting or upsizing buffers. Increasing slew margin causes proactive buffering before violations become critical.

OpenRAM-generated SRAM macros have unrealistically tight max_transition values (e.g. 0.04ns) on inputs due to analytical model pessimism. Insert dedicated clock-grade buffers (clkbuf_4 or buf_6) on all SRAM address/data/control input pins. Known OpenRAM liberty model limitation.

Net load capacitance exceeds library limits, causing signal integrity issues. Inserting repeater buffers on long wires reduces capacitance per driver. Reducing MAX_WIRE_LENGTH forces earlier buffering before violations accumulate.

OpenLane.PL_RESIZER_MAX_SLEW_MARGIN: increase to handle residual high-fanout nets

rules.explanation: High fanout nets drive too many loads, increasing capacitance and degrading transitions. Reduce SYNTH_MAX_FANOUT so Yosys inserts buffers earlier. For global reset/scan_enable signals, use dedicated high-drive-strength buffers.

Long metal wires accumulate charge during fabrication, damaging gate oxides (antenna effect). Strategy 3 uses OpenROAD automatic diode insertion during global routing. Increasing iterations allows the router to find and fix more violations.

error_keywords: persistent antenna violations after diode insertion

OpenLane.PL_TARGET_DENSITY: reduce slightly to give router room to insert diodes

rules.explanation: When strategy 3 fails, switch to strategy 4 (insert fake diodes pre-placement, swap real ones post-routing) or strategy 5 (combined). Reducing density creates routing room for diode cells.

DRC violations indicate the layout does not meet foundry design rules. Metal width/spacing/area violations often come from routing under congestion on lower layers. Reducing density helps the router choose cleaner paths. li.6 (local interconnect area) violations in Sky130 may be a known PDK artifact.

ORFS_ASAP7.note: Many ASAP7 DRC errors stem from incomplete tech LEF definitions (known open PDK issue). Verify against asap7_drm_201207a.pdf.

rules.explanation: ASAP7 DRC violations like V2.M3.AUX.2 (via must match M3 width, not M2) are known issues in the open PDK tech LEF. Many are artifacts of incomplete PDK definitions, not real electrical violations. Verify against the official ASAP7 design rule manual.

Metal shorts and spacing violations in detailed routing are secondary effects of congestion — the router deviates from preferred paths and causes DRCs. Fix upstream congestion first by reducing density and increasing GRT adjustment.

LVS mismatch means the extracted layout netlist does not match the schematic. Common causes: missing power connections (VDD/VSS not connected to cell pins), cells added/removed by optimization, or macro power pin mismatches. Enable LVS_INSERT_POWER_PINS.

OpenLane.SYNTH_ELABORATE_ONLY: 0 (disable - it can skip power pin insertion)

rules.explanation: Power pin mismatches in user_project_wrapper occur when VDD/GND rails are not stitched to macros. Enable LVS_INSERT_POWER_PINS. Disable SYNTH_ELABORATE_ONLY which can prevent proper PDN connections.

error_keywords: logic cells in wrapper LVS mismatch
rules.explanation: At the top-level wrapper, resizer optimizations can add unexpected cells that break LVS. Disable design optimizations at the wrapper level; individual hardened macros should already be optimized.

OpenLane.CTS_MAX_CAP: check vs root buffer output cap limit

rules.explanation: Clock tree cannot balance skew within the target. Relax the skew target first to get a legal CTS solution, then tighten gradually. Ensure a mix of buffer sizes (clkbuf_2, 4, 8, 16) is available for fine-grain balancing.

OpenLane.CTS_ROOT_BUFFER: upgrade to clkbuf_16 for lower latency
OpenLane.FP_CORE_UTIL: reduce to improve clock routing paths

rules.explanation: High clock insertion delay (latency) means clock paths are long. Use a stronger root buffer (clkbuf_16) and ensure the floorplan is not overly congested so clock nets can take direct paths from source to sinks.

error_keywords: CTS buffer insertion caused hold violation
rules.explanation: After CTS, newly inserted clock buffers change path delays and introduce hold violations. This is expected. Enable post-CTS hold fixing with the resizer and set an appropriate slack margin.

OpenLane.CLOCK_PORT: verify correct port name (e.g. clk, CLK)

rules.explanation: CTS fails if no clock is defined in the constraints. Verify the SDC file contains create_clock with the correct clock port name and period. CLOCK_PORT must match the actual RTL input port name exactly.

CTS inserts many clock buffers which need physical space. If placement is already dense, buffer insertion worsens congestion. Reduce target placement density before CTS to leave room for clock buffers.

adjustments.FP_PDN_VPITCH: reduce to add more vertical straps
adjustments.FP_PDN_HPITCH: reduce to add more horizontal straps

ORFS.PDN_TCL: edit to increase strap density and width

rules.explanation: Insufficient power delivery causes IR drop violations. Reduce strap pitch (denser grid) and increase strap width to lower power rail resistance, improving uniform current delivery to all standard cells.

Power net names must exactly match the netlist and LEF. Verify VDD_NETS and GND_NETS match the stdcell library power pin names. Enable core ring to provide a continuous power loop around the design perimeter.

OpenLane.DECAP_CELL: ensure decap cells are in SCL library and enabled

rules.explanation: Dynamic IR drop from simultaneous cell switching. Mitigate by inserting decoupling capacitor cells near high-switching regions (especially clock buffers), spatially spreading simultaneously switching logic, and densifying the PDN mesh.

OpenLane.FP_ASPECT_RATIO: adjust to 1.0 for a square die

rules.explanation: Floorplan fails when the die area is too small to accommodate all macros and standard cells. Reduce core utilization or explicitly increase the die area. 40% utilization is a safe baseline for complex designs.

Legalization moves cells to legal grid positions after global placement. Cell overlaps after legalization typically mean density is too high. Reduce target density to give the legalizer room to spread cells.

Macros (SRAMs, IP blocks) must be placed at legal boundary-aligned positions with sufficient halo. Automatic macro placement often fails for complex designs. Provide a manual placement file with macros oriented pins-facing-inward to ease routing.

OpenLane.FP_TAPCELL_DIST: reduce to meet max tap spacing DRC (Sky130: typically 14-20um)

rules.explanation: Tap cells provide well contacts for latch-up prevention. Sky130 requires tap cells within ~14um of every transistor. Verify FP_TAPCELL_DIST matches the PDK requirement and tap cell insertion is enabled.
IO pin placement fails when pins conflict with PDN straps or macro blockages. Switch to equidistant mode (FP_IO_MODE=1). Verify H and V pin metal layers do not conflict with power straps.

OpenLane.SYNTH_TOP: verify top module name matches Verilog exactly
OpenLane.VERILOG_FILES: verify all source files are listed

rules.explanation: Synthesis failures are usually caused by unresolved module references, file path errors, or RTL syntax issues. Verify all Verilog source files are included, the top module name matches exactly, and all submodules are defined or black-boxed.

Post-synthesis area is too large. Switch synthesis strategy to area-focused (AREA 0 or AREA 1). Disabling automatic buffering reduces area at the cost of potential fanout violations resolved during placement.

OpenLane.BASE_SDC_FILE: verify constraint file path and contents

rules.explanation: SDC constraint errors halt synthesis. Clock port names must match RTL ports exactly. Add clock uncertainty (jitter) and transition margins appropriate for the target process.

Inferred latches or combinational loops in RTL cause synthesis issues and downstream hold violations. Fix in RTL: ensure all if-else branches are complete, add default assignments to all outputs, and break combinational loops with registered stages.

C++ engine fault (AVX/Memory). Marginally shifting the floorplan alters the optimization seed and may bypass the math fault. Also update the OpenROAD/OpenLane Docker image to the latest version, as many crashes are fixed in newer releases.

OpenLane.ROUTING_CORES: reduce threads to lower peak memory

rules.explanation: Out-of-memory during routing or placement. Reduce parallel routing threads (ROUTING_CORES) to lower peak memory usage. For very large designs, limit routing layers or split hierarchically.

config_params.fix: docker pull efabless/openlane:latest && cd OpenLane && make mount

rules.explanation: Docker environment issue. Pull the latest OpenLane Docker image and remount. Ensure the Docker daemon is running and the current user is in the docker group.

error_keywords: make: *** No rule to make target

ORFS.env: source setup_env.sh in every new terminal

rules.explanation: ORFS Makefile cannot find the design config or ORFS is not built. Verify DESIGN_CONFIG path, ensure build_openroad.sh was executed, and source setup_env.sh before every make invocation.

OpenLane.RCX_RULES: verify PDK RCX rules file exists

rules.explanation: SPEF extraction provides real wire parasitics for post-layout STA. If OpenRCX fails, verify the PDK includes RCX rule files. Without SPEF, timing analysis uses ideal wire models and will miss real post-route violations.

Post-route STA at worst-case corners (slow-max, fast-min) may fail even when pre-route timing passed. Increase clock uncertainty margin in SDC, enable resizer optimizations at placement and global route stages, and run multi-corner STA.

GDS streaming issues often relate to layout coordinate problems. Zeroize the origin in Magic before streaming out. Ensure all cell views are present and correctly merged. Use KLayout as a secondary GDS viewer and DRC checker.

Metal density fill is required for CMP (chemical mechanical planarization) uniformity. Enable fill insertion. If it fails, verify routing layers have adequate free space and that fill cell LEF is available in the PDK.

OpenLane.CVC_SCRIPTS_DIR: provide correct CVC scripts for multi-voltage designs

rules.explanation: CVC validates power domain crossings and gate oxide stress. For single-voltage-domain designs, CVC failures are often due to incorrect power domain definitions. Provide correct power intent or disable CVC for single-voltage designs.

ORFS_ASAP7.TECH_LEF: verify asap7sc7p5t_27 or asap7sc7p5t_28 tech LEF

rules.explanation: ASAP7 has multiple cell library variants (6.5-track and 7.5-track, v26/v27/v28). Mismatched tech LEF and liberty files cause floorplan errors. Ensure TECH_LEF, LIB_FILES, and PLACE_SITE all reference the same ASAP7 variant and version.

metadata.description: Yunair Empire - ASAP7 & ORFS Predictive Fixes

rules.explanation: Setup timing violations on ASAP7 typically indicate cell clustering and transition degradation. Reducing utilization gives the placer more space to insert repeaters and size up driving cells.
7nm pin access is severely restricted. High place density causes local pin congestion and DRC failures. Decreasing PLACE_DENSITY forces the tool to spread standard cells.

nwell.4 with a small violation count and the distinctive "Should be divided by 3 or 4" Magic-internal hint is the signature of a documented upstream OpenROAD tapcell-insertion limitation (github.com/The-OpenROAD-Project/OpenROAD issue #7118, "tap deserts"), not a real design defect. Empirically confirmed across 4 different FP_TAPCELL_DIST values (15/10/7/20) and 2 different floorplan strategies (absolute 1500x1500 and relative ~105x103) on a real design tonight -- the violation box stayed exactly 0.840um x 1.655um every time, which is the signature of a fixed tool-level artifact, not something that responds to config tuning. Given LVS and routing-stage DRC are unaffected, forcing QUIT_ON_MAGIC_DRC off for this specific signature lets the flow complete instead of chasing a config value that provably will not fix it.
